--- title: trend --- ```python trend( data, variable, *, by=None, units=True, stat='mean', max_units=400, title=None, ref=None, ) ``` A variable over time: its mean (or median) across units, with a band, and each unit's path. ## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} | Name | Type | Description | Default | |-----------|-------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------| | data | | A dataset id, or a panel with ``geo_id`` and ``year``, e.g. from ``load`` | _required_ | | variable | str | The numeric column to follow | _required_ | | by | str \| None | One line per group: a column of the table, or a coarser scale of its units (e.g. the first-level administrative scale), whose names are added | `None` | | units | bool | Draw each unit's own trajectory as a thin grey line behind the summary | `True` | | stat | str | ``"mean"`` (band: one standard error on each side) or ``"median"`` (band: the interquartile range) | `'mean'` | | max_units | int | Draw at most this many unit trajectories (a reproducible random sample when there are more); the statistics always use every unit | `400` | | title | str \| None | The figure title | `None` | ## Notes {.doc-section .doc-section-notes} The panel needs at least two years with data. ## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns} | Name | Type | Description | |--------|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | | TrendResult | A result with ``.df`` (one row per year and group: the statistic in a column named ``mean`` or ``median``, the band in ``lower`` and ``upper``, and ``n`` units), ``.fig``, ``.first`` and ``.last`` (years), ``.value_first``, ``.value_last`` and ``.change`` (the statistic across all units), ``.share_rising`` (share of units with data in both years that ended higher), ``.n_units``, ``.notes`` and ``.interpret()``. | ## Example {.doc-section .doc-section-example} ```python !pip install -q geo4bolivia import geo4bolivia as geo res = geo.trend("ntl", "ln_NTLpc") print(res.interpret()) res.fig ``` ::: {.g4-example-links} [Open a blank Colab notebook to run it](https://colab.research.google.com/notebooks/empty.ipynb) ::: ::: {#7da7560d .cell execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display .cell-output-markdown} Between 2012 and 2020, the mean of **Log night-time lights per capita** across 331 units rose from 13.1 to 13.9 (a change of +0.812). 94% of the units with data in both years ended higher than they started: the summary line describes the typical unit, not every unit. The band is one standard error on each side of the mean: how precisely the average is known, not how much units differ. _These are associations, not causal effects. A causal reading needs a research design._ ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
